newsitem.title: USA: Freeze losses seen for Texas HRW wheat - agronomist.
newsitem.headline: Freeze losses seen for Texas HRW wheat - agronomist.

text.p: The hard red winter wheat crop in Texas is likely to suffer major losses following a sharp drop in temperatures over the weekend, said Travis Miller, agronomist at Texas A&M University.
"This (wheat crop) was looking very good and it has been hammered with the cold weather and I am sure we will have major losses," he said.
Miller, an extension small grains specialist, said Texas would now probably not even get an average crop this year.
He noted the Texas crop was more susceptible to freeze damage than other states as its development was more advanced.
"The further along you are in development the more likely cold temperatures are going to cause loss of wheat," he said.

Miller said wheat would be hurt in the two major growing areas, the northern Panhandle and High Plains (around Wichita Falls). In the former, wheat was in the jointing to second joint stage and in the latter it was in boot stage or headed.
He noted around Wichita Falls, where the wheat is knee high, temperatures fell to about 24 to 25 degrees Fahrenheit.
"If that is frozen out, chances are there won't be much left," Miller said, noting a mild winter had left the wheat more advanced than normal for the time of year.
Further north, temperatures were colder, falling into the teens F, but the wheat was less advanced.

"With some Panhandle wheat, it may be second and third tillers make some wheat but the main stem tiller doesn't," he said, noting in around seven days it would be possible to make a more accurate damage estimate.
Last year Texas produced 75 million bushels of winter wheat, making it the fourth largest U.S. winter wheat state, according to U.S. Department of Agriculture data.
